Subject: Proposed dependency upgrades for our Redwood Private cluster

Hi Sergio —

Were planning a coordinated maintenance for our on-prem Redwood Private deployment (cluster ID: AA-PRIV-02). Our infra team needs to bump a couple of infra-level packages that Redwood bundles in the private appliance (containerd runtime 1.7.x -> 1.8.x, glibc security backports, and the kernel driver set used with our NICs). The customer-side goal is to get the infra patched without introducing service regressions.

Before we pick calendar dates, two asks from us:
- Can Redwood provide a clearly documented fallback procedure that unpins to the prior service image within 30 minutes if we see errors?
- We need a short preflight checklist and an assurance that the private package pins will be honored (no auto-upgrade on your side).

Proposed maintenance window: week of Nov 29 (US PST preferred), 2–4 hours in the low-traffic night window. Were open to a canary-first approach.

What we need from you: high-level runbook, rollback steps we can validate during a dry run, and the expected SLO impact for a canary (p95 latency, CPU/GPU footprint).

Thanks — Samira
Samira Nolan

Samira — thanks for the heads up. Short answers first: yes, we will provide a rollback playbook and we will honor version pinning for your private deployment (we do not push runtime or model updates without an explicit version pin/per-deployment consent).

Plan sketch:
1) Preflight (dry run) in your non-prod environment on Nov 23 — well run the checklist and a simulated canary with traffic replay.
2) Production window options: Nov 30 01:00–03:00 PST or Dec 2 02:00–04:00 PST. We recommend the Nov 30 slot to keep prep time short.
3) Canary strategy: 3 nodes (10% of capacity) across two racks, 30-minute steady-state observation using the canary-matrix. If no regressions, progressive rollout in 20% increments with 15-minute holds.
4) Rollback guardrails: image tags with immutable manifest (sha-based tag), pre-pulled previous image kept for 48 hours, and kube-rollout undo script that can revert a deployment to the previous replica set.

Next steps:
- Marcus (cc) will provide the concrete commands and the playbook draft.
- Can you confirm which of the two windows you prefer and whether you want us to run the dry run on Nov 23 or a day earlier?

I attached the preflight checklist you sent and will attach our rollback playbook draft once Marcus finishes it.

— Sergio

Subject: Re: Proposed dependency upgrades for our Redwood Private cluster — rollback playbook (draft)

Hi team — draft of the technical rollback and safety steps below. This is tailored for the private appliance pattern (systemd units + k8s static manifests).

High-level constraints
- No DB schema changes allowed during the maintenance window. Any data migrations must be feature-flagged and reversible.
- Network ACL changes will be staged and validated via a canary VM before clusterwide apply.

Immediate rollback knobs (order matters):
1) Pause ingress: run "/opt/redwood/bin/control pause-ingress --cluster AA-PRIV-02" to stop new external requests to the cluster.
2) Switch traffic to fallback pool: update the load-balancer weight to favor the fallback pool (LB API call: POST /lb/pools/fallback/weight).
3) K8s undo (fast path): 
   - kubectl -n redwood rollout undo deployment/inference-runtime --to-revision=$(kubectl -n redwood rollout history deployment/inference-runtime -o yaml | grep Revision: | head -n1 | awk '{print $2}')
   - kubectl -n redwood rollout status deployment/inference-runtime -w (watch until stable)
4) Container runtime fallback: if containerd upgrade causes native crashes, rollback the containerd systemd unit to the pre-upgrade RPM: 
   - rpm -Uvh --oldpackage /var/backups/rpms/containerd-1.7.12.rpm
   - systemctl restart containerd
5) Network driver rollback: staging kernel module unload/load sequence (we keep vendor-signed versions in /opt/redwood/drivers/).

Validation checks (post-rollback, 15 mins):
- inference p95 < 1.5x baseline and error rate < 0.5% absolute increase
- KV cache hit ratio within 90% of baseline
- No pod restarts beyond expected (see canary-matrix.csv thresholds)

Preflight dry-run checklist (short):
- Confirm image immutability (sha tags) and registry access
- Confirm prior images are pre-pulled on each node (/var/lib/containers/prepull-list.yaml)
- Verify monitoring alerts hooked into the canary SLA dashboard

Attachments (drafts): private-rollback-playbook.md, canary-matrix.csv

If we need a faster hard-fallback, we can switch traffic to the dedicated fallback pool and then perform a rolling restart into the prior image; that path is a 20–30 minute operation in my tests.

— Marcus Lin
Infra Reliability, Redwood Inference
